title: ControlTraj: Controllable Trajectory Generation with Topology-Constrained Diffusion Model

problem.claim: Trajectory data generation can help address privacy concerns, collection costs, and proprietary restrictions in human mobility analysis.

gap.claim: Existing trajectory generation methods struggle with fidelity, flexibility, and generalizability because human activities are diverse and unpredictable.

contributions.claim: ControlTraj is a controllable trajectory generation framework based on a topology-constrained diffusion model.
The framework introduces a road segment autoencoder for extracting fine-grained road segment embeddings.
GeoUNet merges encoded road features with trip attributes to synthesize geographic trajectories from white noise.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across three real-world data settings, the authors report that ControlTraj generates human-directed, high-fidelity trajectories.
The authors report adaptability to unexplored geographical contexts.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generated trajectory data may reduce privacy, collection-cost, and proprietary-access constraints in human mobility analysis.
Existing methods remain limited in fidelity, flexibility, and generalizability due to the diversity and unpredictability of human activities.
ControlTraj applies a topology-constrained diffusion model, a road segment autoencoder, and the GeoUNet architecture conditioned on trip attributes.
Experiments across three real-world data settings are reported to demonstrate human-directed, high-fidelity generation and adaptability to unexplored geographic contexts.

source_observation.claim: The method combines learned trajectory generation with explicit road-network topology constraints.

interpretation.claim: Domain structure can be incorporated into generative modeling to guide geographically plausible outputs.

application.claim: For structured spatial sequence generation, consider conditioning or constraining the generator with relevant network topology.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether topology constraints improve results relative to unconstrained alternatives in all settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail the control interface, topology-constraint mechanism, or limitations across geographic contexts.
